text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Top court tosses out sex case: Judges split, 5-4, to halt prosecution of teacher because rape crisis centre shredded notes.
- Need for big cuts ebbing, Eves says: Tax revenue up, deficit down, growth higher than expected.
- Markets expect few budget surprises: Minor rise in federal spending, aid for charity and child poverty forecast.
- Ottawa eyes curb on entry of strippers: Federal letter suggest closing loophole.
- Corporate cash registers ring in Chinese New Year: Companies are eager to woo the burgeoning power of Asian immigrants by sponsoring a celebration that used to be little known in Canada.
- OSC stalls Morrison takeover: Oil firm gains reprieve as regulator to determine whether Canadian 88 bid breaks rules.
- Eggleton delays challenge of Helms-Burton: Waiting for EU trade case against U.S.
- Vancouver celebrates the man they call Uncle Wing.
- Beatrice to be sold for C$440-million: Dairy says surprise deal set for April.

- OSC suspends Morrison trades: Hearing next week will look into Canadian 88's ties with West Central Capital -- a move that could derail C$652-million hostile bid for Morrison. Canadian 88 says bid expires today anyway.
- Wheat pools grab 13 percent of United Grain Growers to shield farmers.
